contexts.text: In the Spiritual World they are satisfied [in appetite] with truths and goods...
In our eating bread to satiety () = enjoy the good of pleasures as much as they wanted. AC 8432. AC 8448.
For the will is what is satisfied with good with the good, and with evil with the evil.
Ye shall eat fat to satiety... Ye shall be satisfied upon my table (). Explained. AE 355:2. AE 617:25.
All the birds were filled with their flesh () = that the infernal Genii are as it were fed with their concupiscences...
Like burdening a table with food after satiety.
To satisfy every living thing with good pleasure () = to enrich all who receive life from Him with Divine truth from love.
The dogs... do not know satiety () = cannot receive good. Satiety = the reception of good; for satiety is predicated of food, by which is signified spiritual nourishment.
Not to be satisfied () = not to find truth which in itself is truth.
To eat and not be satisfied () = because truth from good is so little and so rare that it will yield scarcely any nourishment for the soul.

Wherefore do ye spend... your labour for that which is not for satiety? () = that it is in vain to procure for ourselves from proprium that which nourishes the soul... Satiety = that which nourishes the soul; here, that which does not nourish it. (Further illustrated.)
To eat to satiety () = plenary reception, perception, and appropriation.
Satiety of bread () = contempt for all the good and truth of Heaven and the Church, and nausea at them.
No satiety for thee () = the cupidity of falsifying truths without end.
